extracted.intended_audience: licensees, applicants, and counsel in the FCC Wireless Radio Services (and FCC staff processing those applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and evaluation standards governing applications, modifications, transfers/assignments, renewals, partitioning/disaggregation, discontinuance, and related procedures for Wireless Radio Services under 47 CFR Part 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant criteria for applications (public interest and non-preclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: A grant of the application would not preclude the grant of any mutually exclusive application; and a grant of the application would serve the public interest, convenience, and necessity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These findings are part of the Commission's determination whether to grant an application (see surrounding provisions for other prerequisites to grant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant of petitioned applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The FCC may grant, without a formal hearing, an application against which petition(s) to deny have been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition(s) to deny are pending when an application is granted, the FCC will deny the petition(s) and issue a concise statement of the reason(s) for the denial, disposing of all substantive issues raised in the petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial and conditional grants
rubrics_metrics.description: The FCC may grant applications in part, and/or subject to conditions other than those normally applied to authorizations of the same type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When issuing partial or conditional grants the FCC will inform the applicant of the reasons. Such partial or conditional grants are final unless the FCC revises its action in response to a petition for reconsideration. Such petitions must be filed by the applicant within thirty days after the letter or order stating the reasons, and must reject the partial or conditional grant and return the instrument of authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation for hearing when findings cannot be made
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission is unable to make the prescribed findings it will designate the application for hearing and notify applicant and known parties in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders designating applications for hearing will specify with particularity the matters in issue. Parties not initially notified may petition for intervention within 30 days after publication in the Federal Register. Applicant and all parties shall be permitted to participate; hearings may be conducted by the Commission, the Chief of the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau, or an Administrative Law Judge. Burden of proceeding and proof generally rests on the applicant, except as otherwise determined with respect to issues presented by petitions to deny or petitions to enlarge the issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and commencement of service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Wireless Radio Service has requirements for construction and commencement of service or operations as set forth in the rule part governing the specific service; the period between grant and required commencement is the construction period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants/licensees must follow the specific service rules for construction/commencement; see service-specific rule parts for timeframes and technical requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage and substantial service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain Wireless Radio Services impose geographic coverage or substantial service requirements within a specified time period; the period between grant and that required degree of coverage/substantial service is the coverage period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage/substantial service obligations and timeframes are specified in the service-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic termination for failure to construct or meet coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: If a licensee fails to commence service by the expiration of its construction period or to meet coverage/substantial service obligations by the expiration of its coverage period, its authorization terminates automatically (in whole or in part) on the date the period expires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination occurs without specific Commission action; service rules may specify partial terminations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee notification of compliance (Form 601)
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee who commences service/operations within the construction period or meets its coverage/substantial service obligations must notify the Commission by filing FCC Form 601 within 15 days of the expiration of the applicable construction or coverage period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For site-specific authorizations, if some but not all authorized transmitters are in service, the notification must show which transmitters it applies to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for extension of construction or coverage periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees may request to extend a construction or coverage period by filing FCC Form 601 before the expiration of the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions may be granted if failure to meet the deadline is due to involuntary loss of site or causes beyond control. Extensions are not granted for failures due to lack of financing, lack of antenna site, or ordering equipment late (except a presumption of diligence if equipment was ordered within 90 days of initial grant). Extensions are not granted for transfer of control or to allow transferee/assignee to complete facilities not constructed by transferor. Filing an extension request does not automatically extend the period unless based on involuntary loss of site or similar circumstances, in which case the construction period is automatically extended pending disposition. An extension for one transmitter does not extend the construction period for other transmitters/facilities under the same authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major vs minor license modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: All major modifications (as defined in §1.929) require prior Commission approval and are treated as new applications for filing date, Public Notice, and petition to deny purposes; minor modifications (other than pro forma transfers/assignments) may be made as a matter of right without prior Commission approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where other rules permit permissive changes to technical parameters without notifying the Commission (e.g., adding/modifying/deleting internal sites), no notification is required. For other minor modifications (e.g., contact info changes), licensees must notify the Commission by filing FCC Form 601 within 30 days of implementing such changes. Multiple pending modification applications requesting changes to the same/related technical parameters are not permitted; additional changes must be made as an amendment to the pending modification application. Modifications requiring a fee must be filed in accordance with §1.913.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule for assignment of authorization/transfer of control
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizations in the Wireless Radio Services may be assigned or control transferred only upon application to and approval by the Commission, except as provided in the section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The general rule applies to voluntary/involuntary assignments and direct/indirect transfers; exceptions and specific procedures follow in the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change to 50% or greater ownership equals transfer of control
rubrics_metrics.description: A change from less than 50% ownership to 50% or more ownership shall always be considered a transfer of control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other situations are determined case-by-case considering ownership distribution and relationships (including family relationships).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Entities compliance on transfers/assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated Entities (as defined in §1.2110(a)) must comply with §§1.2110 and 1.2111 when seeking to assign or transfer control of an authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service-specific transfer/assignment rules also apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application requirement for assignment/transfer (Form 603 and Form 602)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignor must file FCC Form 603 for approval of assignment; if assignee/transferee is subject to ownership reporting requirements of §1.2112, the assignee/transferee must file an updated FCC Form 602 or certify a current Form 602 is on file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules for pro forma transfers, involuntary assignments, and timing of filings are detailed in subsequent paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro forma transfer/assignment exceptions for telecommunications carriers
rubrics_metrics.description: For a non-substantial (pro forma) transfer or assignment involving a telecommunications carrier, prior filing and Commission approval are not required if: the affected license is not subject to unjust enrichment provisions under subpart Q; the transfer/assignment does not involve a proxy contest; and the transferee/assignee files Form 603 within 30 days after completion and updates Form 602 as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is limited to the specific conditions listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of involuntary assignment filings
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of an involuntary assignment or transfer, FCC Form 603 must be filed no later than 30 days after the event causing the involuntary assignment or transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes assignments due to death, bankruptcy, or legal disability; other procedural requirements may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of consummation timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees must notify the Commission of consummation of an approved transfer/assignment using FCC Form 603. For transactions requiring prior Commission approval, consummation must occur and notification provided within 180 days of public notice of approval; notification must occur no later than 30 days after actual consummation unless an extension is requested before the 180-day period expires. For transactions not requiring prior approval, notification must be provided on Form 603 no later than 30 days after consummation, with ownership updates on Form 602.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignee/transferee is responsible for providing notification and the date of consummation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial assignment of authorization (partial facility transfers)
rubrics_metrics.description: If some, but not all, facilities of a radio station are assigned to another party, such action is a partial assignment of authorization; to request approval the assignor must notify the Commission on FCC Form 603 of facilities that will be deleted upon consummation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partitioning and disaggregation are treated as requests for partial assignment (see separate rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partitioning and disaggregation treated as partial assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: When a licensee proposes to partition or disaggregate a portion of its authorization, the application will be treated as a request for partial assignment of authorization and the assignor must notify the Commission on FCC Form 603 of the geographic area or spectrum to be deleted upon consummation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.950 for additional definitions, eligibility, filing, and performance requirement rules for partitioning/disaggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involuntary transfer and assignment after death or legal disability
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of death or legal disability of a permittee/licensee or certain controlling persons, the Commission must be notified promptly and within 30 days an application filed for consent to involuntary assignment or transfer of control to a person/entity legally qualified to succeed under applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures/forms are the same as in §1.948(b). For certain services (Ship, aircraft, Commercial Operator, Amateur, and Personal Radio Services except 218-219 MHz) involuntary assignment will not be granted; such licenses shall be surrendered. Amateur call signs of a deceased licensee shall be available for reassignment per §97.19.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure requirements for auctionable services
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for transfer or assignment of licenses in auctionable services must comply with the disclosure requirements of §§1.2111 and 1.2112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those sections address disclosure of bidding credits, installment payments, and ownership interests, among other requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trafficking review and evidentiary showing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for approval of assignment or transfer may be reviewed to determine if the transaction is for purposes of trafficking in service authorizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trafficking is obtaining an authorization principally for speculation or profitable resale rather than to provide services. The Commission may require an affirmative factual showing, supported by affidavit(s), demonstrating the assignor did not acquire the authorization principally for speculation or resale; examples include demonstration of changed circumstances affecting the licensee, or that the assignment is incidental to sale of other facilities or a merger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of assignment/transfer applications (general approval procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications processed under general approval procedures must be sufficiently complete, contain all necessary information/certifications on Form 603 (including eligibility, basic qualifications, foreign ownership), and include payment of required fees; once accepted they will be placed on public notice (except Private Wireless Services). Petitions to deny must comply with §1.939 and be filed within 14 days after public notice of acceptance for filing. The Bureau will act (consent/deny/subject for further review) no later than 21 days following public notice of acceptance for filing (or 21 days after filing if no prior public notice required). If subject to further review, the Bureau will act within 90 days of that public notice or provide notice of additional 90-day review period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent is not deemed granted until the Bureau affirmatively acts; grants are reflected in public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate approval procedures and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that meet specified additional qualifications may qualify for immediate approval procedures: the application must be complete and establish by certifications that (A) the license does not involve spectrum that could be used for interconnected mobile voice/data services creating geographic overlap with spectrum in which the proposed assignee already holds ≥10% interest; (B) the licensee is not a designated entity subject to unjust enrichment/transfer restrictions; (C) the assignment/transfer does not require waiver/declaratory ruling and no pending revocation/cancellation/termination issue exists; and (D) the assignment does not involve a transaction in the Enhanced Competition Incentive Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application establishes these elements consent will be reflected in ULS on the next business day after filing (or after data entry for manual filings). Consent is subject to reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for renewal of authorizations must be filed no later than the expiration date and no sooner than 90 days prior; renewal applications must be filed on the same form as initial authorizations (FCC Form 601 or 605).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees with multiple authorizations in the same service may request a common expiration date for renewal purposes; license terms may be shortened by up to one year but not extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal Standard (Covered Site-based and Covered Geographic Licenses)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant for renewal must demonstrate that over the license term the licensee(s) provided and continue to provide service to the public, or operated and continue to operate the license to meet private, internal communications needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the substantive test the Commission uses to decide renewals for covered licenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbors for meeting the Renewal Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant will meet the Renewal Standard if it can certify that it satisfied one of the enumerated safe harbors (varying by license type): Covered Site-based Licenses (operate consistent with most recently filed construction notification or no permanent discontinuance), Geographic commercial licenses (met interim/final performance requirements and no permanent discontinuance), Geographic private systems (met performance requirements or continued use to further private/public interest/public safety needs and no permanent discontinuance), Partitioned/disaggregated licenses without performance requirement (continues to use facilities and no permanent discontinuance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each safe harbor has specific certification language and applicability depending on license type and whether in initial or subsequent license terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal Showing content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If unable to meet a safe harbor, applicant must make a Renewal Showing addressing the Renewal Standard by including a detailed description of provision of service (or use for private communications) during the entire license period, and addressing as applicable: level and quality of service (population/area/subscribers/services), date service commenced and any interruptions/duration, service to rural areas, service to qualifying tribal land, and any other factors associated with level of service to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Renewal Showing must specifically address the Renewal Standard independent of performance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Compliance Certification for renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant for renewal of an authorization identified under the Renewal Standard must make a Regulatory Compliance Certification that it has substantially complied with all applicable FCC rules, policies, and the Communications Act of 1934, as amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insufficient certifications can be a basis for denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of renewal denial
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission or Bureau finds the licensee has not met the Renewal Standard or the Regulatory Compliance Certification is insufficient, the renewal application will be denied and the licensed spectrum will return automatically to the Commission for reassignment (by auction or other mechanism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For certain site-by-site services spectrum may revert to related overlay geographic-area license holder; AWS-4 licensees holding certain MSS rights may have protections removed in the affected area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for geographic partitioning and spectrum disaggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: County and county equivalent defined by FIPS 6-4; geographic partitioning is assignment of a geographic portion of a geographic area licensee's license area; spectrum disaggregation is assignment of portions of blocks of a geographic area licensee's spectrum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIPS codes and documentation available online (NIST link).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for partitioning and disaggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered Geographic Licenses are eligible for geographic partitioning and spectrum disaggregation, subject to service-specific exceptions (e.g., 220 MHz Service, Cellular Radiotelephone Service, Multichannel Video & Distribution and Data Service restrictions, VHF Public Coast pairing restrictions, and certain bands where disaggregation is not permitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific exceptions listed in §1.950(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements for partitioning/disaggregation (Form 603 and coordinates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties seeking approval must apply for partial assignment of authorization by filing FCC Form 603. Each partitioning request must include an attachment defining the perimeter of the partitioned area by geographic coordinates to the nearest second (NAD83), or may specify an FCC-recognized service area or county/counties, in which case listing the names suffices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate geographic specification is required; NAD83 coordinates or accepted service area names are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relocation of incumbent licensees certification for partitioning/disaggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must, if applicable, include a certification stating which party will meet any incumbent relocation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service-specific rules may modify who is responsible.

rubrics_metrics.name: License term for partitioned/disaggregated licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The license term for a partitioned license area or disaggregated spectrum license is the remainder of the original licensee's license term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purchasers/assignees take the remainder of the original term; renewal/performance obligations attach accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency coordination agreements convey with partial assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any existing frequency coordination agreements convey with the partial assignment and remain in effect for the term of the agreement unless new agreements are reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should account for existing coordination obligations when negotiating partition/disaggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance requirements options for partitioning/disaggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties have two options to satisfy service-specific performance requirements: (1) each party certifies it will individually satisfy requirements and face penalties individually upon failure; or (2) both parties agree to share responsibility, in which case both may be subject to penalties if shared requirements are not met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection of option should be explicit in the partial assignment filings/agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unjust enrichment obligations for partitioning/disaggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees making installment payments or that received a bidding credit who partition or disaggregate to entities that do not meet eligibility standards for installment payments or bidding credits are subject to unjust enrichment requirements of §1.2111.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transactions may trigger repayment or other remedial obligations under unjust enrichment rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to respond to official communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees or applicants receiving official notice of an apparent or actual violation of a federal statute, international agreement, Executive Order, or regulation pertaining to communications shall respond in writing within 10 days to the FCC office originating the notice, unless otherwise specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses must be complete and self-contained without reference to other communications unless copies are attached. Responses may be filed via ULS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinuance of service: automatic termination and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee's authorization will automatically terminate if the licensee permanently discontinues service or operations during the license term. Permanent discontinuance for Covered Geographic Licenses is 180 consecutive days without operation or (for CMRS) providing service to at least one nonaffiliated subscriber; for Covered Site-based Licenses and certain other licenses the rule is 365 consecutive days. Public safety licenses have a 365-day rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channel keepers (test signals, tones, color bars) do not constitute operation or service. Definitions indicate whether an interruption counts as permanent discontinuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirement upon permanent discontinuance
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee that permanently discontinues service as defined must notify the Commission within 10 days by filing FCC Form 601 or 605 requesting license cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An authorization will automatically terminate even if a licensee fails to file the form requesting cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension request for discontinuance period
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee may file a request for a longer discontinuance period for good cause at least 30 days before the end of the applicable 180-day or 365-day discontinuance period. Filing an extension request automatically extends the discontinuance period at least the later of an additional 30 days or until the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau acts on the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early filing (>=30 days before end) is required; the automatic short extension provides time pending Bureau action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorizations remain valid until terminated or revoked
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizations generally remain valid until terminated in accordance with the termination section; however, the Commission may revoke an authorization pursuant to section 312 of the Communications Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination/revocation procedures and grounds are set forth in the applicable statutory and regulatory provisions (section 312 referenced).
